text:
Anna: heads-up — I'm rolling a change to the kernel-selector heuristics + a small deploy-time seeder in staging. want quick eyes on kv key skew and warmup coverage.
Miguel: ack. what's the seeder strategy? full synthetic traffic or prefix-only stubs?
Anna: prefix-only stubs for top-100 prefixes by recent qps. not full synth because we want low cost + predictable kv load.
Jia: pulled profiling from last canary. selector change reduces median p99 compute by 8% for long sequences, but small-batch (b=1-4) increased tail by ~15ms. might affect short prompts hitting cold kv.
Sam: hmm. could we combine: run deploy seeder that writes KV prefixes for top-1000 users, then run a tiny synthetic burst that hits those prefixes only? cheap and gives real hit-rate signal.
Tom: caveat: our keying currently includes user_id + normalized_prompt_prefix. high user cardinality -> high entropy in keys. seeding top prefixes per-user isn't feasible. we need to seed aggregated prefix keys (prefix hash without user) or we'll spray the cache.
Anna: good point. plan is to seed aggregated prefix keys in staging. Tom — can you confirm that code path uses aggregated keying when the env var REDWOOD_SEED_AGGREGATE=true?
Tom: confirmed. staging has REDWOOD_SEED_AGGREGATE=true for this deploy. production will remain user-scoped unless we flip.
runtime-oncall: FYI, staging canary logs after initial seeder run: "kv.fill_rate=0.72 kv-hit=0.18 kv-miss=0.82 seeder_write_ops=980" — that hit rate is low but expected because we only seeded prefixes, not full KV entries for longer context.
Jia: when you say "prefixes" — are we seeding prefix->kv-embedding or prefix->complete-kv? difference matters for hit effectiveness.
Anna: seeder writes compact KV slices (prefix->kv-index) so runtime can splice from existing kv. cheaper than full KV write and should still reduce decode-time misses.
Sam: proposal for experiment steps (short):
1) start seeder in staging (aggregate keys).
2) run 30s synthetic burst targeted at seeded prefixes: `curl -XPOST https://staging.api/redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<seeded_prefix> ...","max_tokens":3}'` with concurrency 8.
3) capture kv-hit, p50/p95/p99 latency and kernel-selection decisions.
4) revert seeder and run same burst as control.
Anna: sounds good. can someone own the metrics dashboard? need quick deltas on kv-hit and small-batch tail.
Miguel: I'll wire a short grafana panel and drop the link here in 10m.
runtime-oncall: small note — autoscaler events can evict recent entries if we spin up fresh nodes; recommend tagging seeder writes with replica_ttl=120s during the test to avoid immediate eviction.
Tom: added — seeder supports replica_ttl flag. default 30s, set to 120s for the run.
Jia: also check kernel-selection logs: we log chosen kernel id per request in /var/log/runtime/kernel.trace. sample: `2026-06-12T09:42:03Z request_id=abc123 kernel=kv-optimized-v2 batch_size=1`. watch for kernel flips during the burst.
Sam: if we see kernel flips + hit-rate drop => likely selector threshold tuned too aggressively for long sequences. fallback: pin kernel for b<=4 to legacy path during rollout.
Anna: ok action items: Miguel->dashboard, Sam->define synthetic payloads (I'll share a seed list), Tom->ensure aggregate keying + replica_ttl=120, Jia->collect kernel traces + perf summary, runtime-oncall->monitor canary and post immediate alerts.
infra-bot: deploy job 9234 finished: staging/runtime:kernel-selector=canary, seeder-image=v2, status=SUCCESS :rocket:
Miguel: linked dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/staging-kv-seed (temp)
Anna: executing seeder now. posting results in ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
runtime-oncall: quick preliminary: after seeder + burst we saw kv-hit jump from 0.18->0.46 for seeded prefixes and p99(b=1) reduced by ~9ms. not final but promising.
Anna: nice. if those numbers hold in longer runs we can propose a play for deploy-time aggregated seeders with replica_ttl=60-180s + optional post-deploy synthetic burst.
Tom: one more guardrail — add a safety throttle to seeder write QPS so we don't spike write amplification on allocator nodes.
Sam: agreed. make seeder default throttle = 200 qps and make it configurable per-deploy.
Anna: perfect. thanks team. I'll open a quick runbook PR and link it here.
Miguel: PR incoming.
Anna: closing loop later with full perf diff. thanks all :thumbsup:
